matches.chunk_text: Scenario | Correct route | Common wrong interpretation Customer disputes CAD 75,000 transfer | Fraud specialist due to unauthorized-transaction indicator. | Treating CAD 75,000 as compensation request. Analyst proposes CAD 1,000.00 compensation | Normal reviewer process; not above threshold. | Using ≥ rather than > threshold. Analyst proposes CAD 1,000.01 | Supervisor approval. | Rounding down or treating as standard. Analyst proposes CAD 10,000.00 | Supervisor approval; not above senior threshold. | Automatically adding senior escalation. Analyst proposes CAD 10,000.01 | Supervisor plus senior escalation. | Using only one approval. Customer threatens regulator and asks for CAD 50 | Compliance route applies despite low amount. | Using amount as sole escalation factor. Old approval for CAD 500; proposal changed to CAD 1,500 | New supervisor approval required. | Reusing stale approval.

This standard defines when a complaint remains with an analyst, when supervisor approval is required, and when specialist or senior escalation is mandatory. It separates the amount or impact described by a customer from a proposed bank action. Mentioning a large disputed transaction does not itself authorize compensation, closure or account action.

Trigger | Specialist route | Immediate constraints | Evidence to capture Unauthorized transaction, stolen card, identity compromise | Fraud specialist | Do not promise reimbursement or disclose sensitive fraud logic. | Transaction identifiers, dates, amount, channel and customer statement. Possible personal-data exposure | Privacy / compliance reviewer | Limit disclosure and preserve incident evidence. | Information involved, discovery time, recipients and actions taken. Legal notice or litigation threat | Legal / compliance reviewer | Do not draft final legal position. | Correspondence reference and relevant history. Regulator correspondence | Compliance reviewer | Preserve attachment/version and audit trail. | Regulator, date, reference and complaint link. Accessibility barrier or accommodation request | Responsible service/human reviewer | Preserve request exactly; do not infer condition. | Requested channel or accommodation and impact. Potential vulnerability expressly described | Human reviewer | Do not diagnose or profile. | Exact customer statement and service impact. Conflicting current policies | Policy owner / compliance | Surface both sources; no automated resolution. | Source IDs, versions and conflicting passages.

results.query: How should a disputed fee be investigated?

matches.chunk_text: Known facts: Routine fee complaint with clear customer/account and current guidance. Required handling: • Retrieve records. • Retrieve relevant policy. • Prepare findings and recommendation. • Use normal review. Expected outcome: Traceable evidence pack. Applicable controls: BR-023, BR-039

Known facts: Two identical monthly fees posted on the same day. Required handling: • Retrieve fee records and product context. • Confirm duplication rather than assuming. • Prepare correction recommendation. • Apply approvals if additional compensation proposed. Expected outcome: Evidence-backed recommendation with citations. Applicable controls: BR-006, BR-008, BR-023

Known facts: Category: Fees and Charges. A duplicate monthly fee was confirmed in structured transaction history. Required handling: • Validate identity and scope. • Retrieve structured records. • Retrieve current policy evidence. • Document limitations and approval route. Expected outcome: Correct duplicate charge; additional compensation below threshold was reviewed normally. Applicable controls: Evidence matched KB-003; outcome human-approved.
